clarification_questions.question: Is there a reference method that can provide comparison values for tumor-boundary assessment?
clarification_questions.decision_it_changes: The acceptance criteria and the feasibility plan (Yes, a laboratory method: plan: calibrate against it and state its own error; No, none yet: plan: a reference measurement campaign comes first)
clarification_questions.why_it_matters: Models can only be as good as the reference values they are built on.

clarification_questions.question: Do you already have numerical acceptance criteria, such as required accuracy or a detection limit?
clarification_questions.decision_it_changes: The acceptance criteria and the feasibility plan (Yes, they are defined: plan: test against the agreed criteria; Not yet: plan: agree numerical criteria before the test)
clarification_questions.why_it_matters: Without them the experiment has no go or no-go criterion.

clarification_questions.question: Over what range must the target variable for tumor-boundary assessment be followed?
clarification_questions.decision_it_changes: The acceptance criteria and the feasibility plan (Narrow, around a set point: plan: sample around the set point; Wide, from low to high: plan: sample the full range)
clarification_questions.why_it_matters: The range decides whether the sensitivity of a method can be enough.

clarification_questions.question: How quickly must a tumor-boundary assessment result be available?
clarification_questions.decision_it_changes: The acceptance criteria and the feasibility plan (Real time, within seconds: plan: a short link and fast sampling; Hours are fine: plan: at-line sampling may be enough)
clarification_questions.why_it_matters: The response time limits the measurement and sampling set-up.

clarification_questions.question: Where could the probe be installed for the proposed measurement?
clarification_questions.decision_it_changes: The acceptance criteria and the feasibility plan
clarification_questions.why_it_matters: Access and cleaning decide the probe geometry and the maintenance effort.

clarification_questions.question: Would the proposed measurement point be hot, under pressure or prone to build-up?
clarification_questions.decision_it_changes: The acceptance criteria and the feasibility plan (Yes, hot, pressurised or fouling: adds risk: a hot or fouling interface)
clarification_questions.why_it_matters: The conditions decide the interface and the probe ratings to confirm.

feasibility_plan.objective: Assess research-stage feasibility for tumor-boundary discrimination on retained tissue samples.
clarify_first: Is there a reference method that gives comparison values?

samples_and_states.text: Select retained tissue samples spanning the client-agreed target range and document their preparation and storage states.

reference_measurements.text: Obtain matched comparison values using a reference method agreed with the client.

setup.text: Acquire MIR, NIR and Raman spectra under documented conditions, recording Raman excitation separately from Raman shift.

comparison.text: Compare each method with the reference assessments against client-agreed criteria set before testing, explicitly accounting for false-negative outcomes.

validation.text: Test each fixed analysis on independent retained samples excluded from its development.

go_no_go.text: Use the agreed criteria to decide whether further research is warranted, not whether to authorize surgical use.

not_demonstrated.text: Clinical performance of the proposed setup, including its false-negative behavior in vivo, remains unknown.

steps: Clarify requirements, reference method and acceptance criteria.

Decide whether results justify further research under agreed criteria.

decision_basis.text: Base research continuation on comparison with reference assessments on independent retained material against criteria agreed with the client before testing.
